blockers.quote: You've done to him exactly what you did to yourself.
blockers.why: Check #11. After the wordless peak, with the chip drained and the bat rolling out of sight, the narrator explains the meaning and the guilt. The picture already shows it. The line also arrives as a lesson at the moment the viewer should be left alone with the image.
blockers.fix: Cut the line and let the held shot of the dark gap under the cupboard carry the beat. If Arthur must speak, use one plain fact that doesn't judge, for example 'He didn't even argue.' [low, flat].

blockers.why: Check #11. The grey chip and the 'zero' are already on screen in the dark window (line 124), so 'Grey. Zero.' narrates what the picture shows. It also pre-empts the hold and the single note that follow.
blockers.fix: Say only 'And Aarav's.' [hushed], then let the hold and the one note finish it. If the number must be heard, keep 'Zero.' and cut 'Grey.'.

suggestions.fix: This reads as a summary of the result over the final image. Replace with a line inside the picture, as the outline had it: 'Row three. You don't look up.' [warm, low]. Then the beat and 'thwack'.

suggestions.quote: You've been wearing the crowd's number like a verdict. But yours moved. Down. Because copying someone's notes was never going to copy their number.
suggestions.fix: Too long for one breath at 1.1x and it reads like an essay. Split it: 'You've been wearing the crowd's number. Like a verdict.' / 'But yours moved. Down.' / 'Copying their notes was never going to copy their number.' [quiet, dawning].

suggestions.quote: Your own chip started from a crowd too. Last year, about one in a thousand UPSC applicants got in (c01).
suggestions.fix: Add the spoken form to say.yaml (U-P-S-C, already planned). Make it two short beats for the ear: 'Your chip started from a crowd too.' / 'Last year? About one in a thousand U-P-S-C applicants got in.' [plain, quiet].

suggestions.quote: The teacher, filling in the form. Again. His three per cent was never about you.
suggestions.fix: 'The teacher, filling in the form' narrates the window shot. Start at the reveal: 'The teacher. Filling in the form, again. His three was never about you.' Cut the picture-description, or make it 'Him? He's sitting the exam. Again.' [amused, soft].

suggestions.quote: The topper, at a keyboard. Her eight was music, all along. A year of notes, copied from someone who doesn't want the exam.
suggestions.fix: Cut 'The topper, at a keyboard.' because the tag MUSIC and the picture show it. Trim to 'Her eight was music, all along. A year of notes... from someone who doesn't want the exam.' [wry, a little rueful]. Add the direction to the narration notes.

suggestions.quote: But his tiny number follows you into the hall. So you look for certainty. The teacher.
suggestions.fix: 'His' is unclear on the first listen (Aarav's chip, said hours of story-time earlier). Say 'But Aarav's tiny number follows you into the hall.' Keep 'The teacher.' as its own take.

suggestions.quote: Row three. The night batch. Your own notes.
suggestions.fix: No delivery direction is given for this line. Add [steady, warm, a little lighter than the opening] so it mirrors the tired opening line as its opposite.

suggestions.quote: At home, Aarav's waiting. A fee slip for a cricket academy. And one question. For the one who can see the numbers.
suggestions.fix: 'For the one who can see the numbers' is the sort of tail that reads off a page. Make it 'And one question. For you. The one who can see the numbers.' or cut it, leaving 'And one question.' [warm, uneasy] before the bubble.

suggestions.quote: A year of fees. A year of your life. On one chair. So... keep going?
suggestions.fix: Direction missing for the pivot to the question. Mark [flat, then a small lift on 'keep going?'] and give 'So...' a breath-length gap.

keep.quote: You can't borrow someone's odds. Only their apron.
The biggest number? It tells you what's likely. It can't tell you what's worth choosing.
